hypothesis: Converting a C-contiguous borrowed mutable buffer to owned bytes is sufficient to create a producer-epoch-consistent Clay Bytes snapshot.
counterhypothesis: Ownership after copy does not establish that all bytes came from one producer epoch when the exporter can mutate concurrently outside the copying process/GIL; an explicit lease/epoch/stability protocol is required before admitting borrowed mutable buffers as canonical Clay Bytes.

bounded_experiment.mechanism: 32 MiB anonymous shared mmap; forked writer alternated full-buffer 0x00/0xff producer epochs while reader materialized bytes(memoryview(mmap)).

interpretation: An owned immutable bytes result can still be a torn cross-epoch snapshot. Copying a borrowed mutable/shared exporter is therefore insufficient as the semantic admission contract for canonical Clay Bytes.

entityos_impact.required_fence: Canonical Clay Bytes should admit already-owned immutable bytes only until an explicit producer lease/epoch/stability contract exists for mutable or borrowed Buffer ingress.
entityos_impact.bytes_buffer_split: Bytes = immutable owned value; Buffer/shared ingress = separate future lease/epoch-aware contract.
